Subaru plans 1.2 million sales to fight tariffs [[n1887]]. Nissan, Honda and Mitsubishi are talking tie-ups with little to show so far [[n1888]]. Automakers are also betting on humanoid robots beyond the assembly line [[n5048]], which is a capex diversion rather than a margin driver.
EPS Upside Watch

The set-up is for a surprise from tariff relief and volume. Volkswagen (VOW3.DE) is up 5.30% over 20 sessions at 104.10 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), and the EPS upside is in its tariff exposure, while the rest of the group carries margin risk into the next prints.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The cut against the bearish narrative is Subaru's volume plan [[n1887]]: a 1.2 million sales target set against tariffs signals that the auto makers are reinvesting for growth rather than retreating, which the margin story does not show.
Narrative

Semis are the sector to own on AI capex, with rotation inside the group. SOXX is up 6.10% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18) and SMH up 5.68%. Micron is at the centre of AI spending as its shares keep soaring [[n3809]], and David Tepper has gone big on Micron, Meta and Alphabet in an AI all-in [[n5005]].
Reported

Analog Devices sees a strong second quarter as AI boom fuels chip sales [[n1934]]. Cadence beat and its stock rose [[n1898]]. Global chip-tool makers are set for double-digit revenue growth [[n4994]].
EPS Upside Watch

Nvidia is the group's surprise candidate. Wells Fargo sees a very positive risk-reward into its earnings [[n1919]], and a Motley Fool piece argues the stock will drop after the Feb. 25 print [[n1916]], which is the bear case the group must clear. Micron is up 15.33% over 20 sessions at 420.95 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), a momentum name with the strongest set-up in the group.
⚡ Breaking Convention

The consensus is to buy Nvidia as the AI-chip leader, but Nvidia sold its entire stake in Arm [[n4983]] and is shaking up its own portfolio by ditching two AI darlings to bet on Intel [[n4985]]. The leadership inside semis is moving to suppliers and to Micron, while the leader is reallocating.

earnings_pattern.title: A beat without a raise gets sold; AI monetisation gets paid
parts: Rewarded

The rewarded names share an AI demand line. Cadence beat and its stock rose [[n1898]]. Figma's shares jumped 15% as the company said AI monetisation is accelerating growth [[n1907]], and DoorDash climbed 14%, reversing a plunge after an earnings and revenue miss [[n1908]]. Analog Devices' stock rose as its chipmaking business boomed [[n1932]], and Kenvue surged on an earnings beat [[n1901]]. Wingstop surged on a beat despite weak same-store sales [[n1899]].
Punished

Beats with a flat outlook were sold. Palo Alto Networks was down 6.5% in the morning, and it had slumped 7% on guidance that fell short [[n1911]] [[n1863]]. Microsoft's largest-ever beat did not stop the stock falling [[n1866]]. Medtronic's better quarter with an unchanged annual outlook also fell [[n1860]]. Zip's shares fell the most since 2014 after a warning on flat earnings [[n1913]], IMCD plunged after a dividend cut and falling revenue [[n1915]], and CRH fell despite a record year after missing estimates [[n1904]].
Pattern

The reaction function is the forward line, with AI demand as the premium. Names with an AI monetisation or chip-demand story rose on a beat (Figma, Analog Devices, Cadence). Names that beat with a flat or cut outlook fell (Microsoft, Palo Alto, Medtronic). A dividend cut or a flat-earnings warning is punished hardest (IMCD, Zip). The earnings beat itself is priced; the forward line decides the direction.
Attention into EPS

Attention is moving to Nvidia's Feb. 25 print [[n1857]]. Wells Fargo sees a very positive risk-reward into the print [[n1919]], while a Motley Fool piece argues the stock will drop after it [[n1916]]. Nvidia is up 5.57% over 20 sessions at 187.98 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18), so the bar has moved up. Software is the other scrutiny point: the sell-off is framed as AI disruption fear [[n5012]].
Playbook

Own the guidance raisers with an AI demand line, and avoid the stocks that beat and then fell, such as Microsoft [[n1866]], until the forward line resets. Into Nvidia, do not pay for a beat: buy the reaction only if the guide is above consensus, and trim on an in-line guide. Position sizing should follow the guide: a raise supports a larger weight, and an in-line guide argues for a smaller one. The call changes if the software sell-off turns guidance cuts into the norm across large caps.

underowned.title: Copper's refining crunch behind the glut
parts: Attention Gap

Copper is treated as a China or global-growth gauge, but in the feed it is an AI and grid-capex asset whose profits are now set by refining. A US copper glut hides a refining crunch [[n5174]], and Antofagasta's profit jumped 52% on record copper prices [[n4898]]. Glencore is stepping up copper growth while its profit slid on the coal slump [[n5170]] [[n5175]]. The attention gap is processing: the refiners and smelters, not the mine price, decide the margin.
Exposure & Risk

Instruments: Freeport-McMoRan (FCX, 62.55, up 4.13% over 20 sessions), the copper future (HG=F, 5.79, up 0.36%) and the materials ETF XLB (up 10.02%), all from Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18. The risk is inventory: a surplus of metal sits in the US, and a copper slide would hit the producers first, while the refiners' bottleneck keeps margins under pressure.
Trigger to Watch

A refining-capacity announcement from a major producer would confirm the processing theme. A sustained draw in the US surplus would show the glut is clearing, which would make the refining crunch the consensus story. Watch for the record copper prices in the producers' reports [[n4898]] as the test.

underowned.title: Data-centre power and the land fight
parts: Attention Gap

The AI trade is crowded in chips, while the power and land bill is under-discussed. A 600-acre AI data centre could cost Wisconsin residents their land [[n5077]], grid technologies are being pitched to meet rising demand [[n5076]], and Zeo Energy signed a deal for 280 MW of power for a Utah data centre [[n5083]]. Efficiency and demand flexibility can meet the load cheaply, according to ACEEE [[n5078]].
Exposure & Risk

Instruments: XLU (up 6.17% over 20 sessions), Vistra (VST, 170.57, up 8.77%) and Constellation Energy (CEG, 294.05, down 0.46%), all from Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18. The risk is local: land-use fights and affordability politics can slow the approvals that the spending plans depend on, and Ford's data-centre plan shows the difficulty [[n5082]].
Trigger to Watch

A land-use or grid-cost decision that makes data-centre builders pay more would turn the utility build-out into a policy trade. Confirmation of the theme comes from a named utility lifting its large-load pipeline, which would make the theme consensus.

underowned.title: Japan's fiscal test and the bond market
parts: Attention Gap

Japan's politics are discussed as a yen story, while the fiscal and bond test gets less coverage. Debt-servicing costs are seen taking 30% of the budget within three years [[n3262]], and two-thirds of firms are concerned about the prime minister's fiscal discipline [[n0858]]. Takaichi faces challenges selling 'proactive' fiscal policy to bond vigilantes [[n3273]], and she is seeking to sell sales-tax and budget pledges after being sworn in [[n3295]].
Exposure & Risk

Instruments: USD/JPY (153.15, down 3.17% over 20 sessions) and the Nikkei 225 (57,143.84, up 7.84%), both from Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18. The risk is that the yen weakens while bond yields rise, which would force the BOJ's hand on the April path [[n3174]] at a point when the IMF is calling for hikes [[n3228]].
Trigger to Watch

The expedited budget deliberation [[n3300]] is the trigger. A budget that keeps spending high while the BOJ tightens would turn the bond market into the theme; a budget framework that narrows the deficit would make the fiscal story consensus in the other direction.

underowned.title: Polish defence money beyond the headline names
parts: Attention Gap

Defence coverage focuses on Poland's buyers, not its listed suppliers. The EU approved €44bn of SAFE loans [[n3393]], and Germany shows interest in the air-defence system [[n3360]]. Northrop Grumman and a Polish partner plan to produce artillery shells in Poland [[n3348]], and the army has banned Chinese cars from its locations [[n3410]]. The English-language headlines rarely tie these programmes to listed Warsaw names.
Exposure & Risk

Instruments: the iShares Poland ETF (EPOL, 37.73, up 5.27% over 20 sessions) and the WIG20 total-return tracker (ETFBW20TR.WA, 67.20, up 3.61%), both from Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18. The link is indirect: the index is dominated by banks and utilities, and the WIG20 has been in a correction [[n3672]].
Trigger to Watch

The parliament's approval of the loans [[n3361]] is the funding step. A first defence export contract for the air-defence system would turn the interest into a company-level earnings story, which is the trigger that makes the theme consensus.

crypto.title: Bitcoin's bounce evaporates below $70,000 as institutions trim
parts: Market Context

Bitcoin closed at 66,425.32, down 21.45% over 20 sessions and down 3.53% over five sessions (prior completed daily close, Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Ether at 1,953.97 is down 30.67% and Solana at 81.57 is down 30.64% over 20 sessions (prior completed daily close, Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The equity proxies fell further: the bitcoin ETF IBIT is down 26.04% at 37.54, Coinbase is down 27.96% at 164.05 and Strategy (MSTR) is down 21.86% at 125.20 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The bounce from this month's crash has evaporated [[n1195]], and bitcoin losing $70,000 is a warning sign [[n1191]].
New / Most Important

Institutions are trimming. Harvard shook up its crypto strategy by selling bitcoin and buying ether [[n1201]], and Brevan Howard cut its bitcoin ETF holding while expanding its options position [[n1222]]. On the other side, Abu Dhabi's Mubadala boosted its bitcoin holdings amid the rout [[n1194]], and Goldman's Solomon says he owns some bitcoin [[n1192]]. Tom Lee says the crypto winter is close to ending [[n1197]], while Nouriel Roubini calls bitcoin 'bogus' and a risk to the financial system [[n1196]].
Playbook

Stance Mixed on bitcoin and Bearish on the levered proxies. Avoid COIN and MSTR over bitcoin itself, since they fell harder over 20 sessions; IBIT is the cleanest exposure if you must hold the asset. The call turns Bullish when accumulation shows in ETF flows, such as the Mubadala add [[n1194]], and bitcoin reclaims $70,000 [[n1191]]. Invalidate the Mixed view on a close below the recent range, which would confirm the next leg down.

flows.title: Liquidity framework: the dollar, the rate checks and credit
parts: Global Liquidity

The balance-sheet question is open. The St. Louis Fed is explaining ample reserves [[n6614]], while the Fed has disclosed that last month's rate checks were at the Treasury's request [[n6620]]. The yen fell amid a broad dollar rally as the Fed confirmed the check [[n2632]], and JPMorgan sees a jump in currency hedging adding to dollar pressure [[n2631]]. The dollar's direction is set by the Fed's willingness to act on the currency, not only by the rate path.
Rates & Dollar

The US 10Y is at 4.09% and the 2Y at 3.47%, a 62 bps spread (US Treasury, prior close 2026-02-18). The dollar index is at 97.70, down 0.95% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). TLT (up 3.32%) and IEF (up 1.52%) both rallied over 20 sessions, while HYG is up 0.04% and LQD is up 1.54%. The FT's read is that the dollar is in doldrums [[n2633]], which is the currency backdrop for the carry trade.
Credit Check

Credit is pricing tight. Hot AT1s hit a new frontier with the tightest-ever euro spread [[n2612]], and KKR's credit strategist is watching spreads and M&A closely [[n2611]]. Disney issued $4bn of corporate bonds for the first time since 2020 [[n2617]]. HYG is flat over 20 sessions (up 0.04%) while LQD is up 1.54%, so high yield is not absorbing new risk at the same pace as investment grade.
Equity & Fund Flows

Hedge funds bought a record amount of Asia equities, Goldman says [[n2504]], and ETF investors are flocking to emerging markets [[n2601]]. Citrone is short US stocks and investing in other areas [[n2606]]. A $54 billion fund manager is quietly being watched for the next flow shift [[n2627]], and Brevan Howard's crypto fund lost 30% in 2025 [[n2626]]. AlphaQuest shut after a three-year losing streak [[n2625]].
Portfolio Implication

Mixed. Keep liquidity exposure in duration and hedged Asia, not in levered credit. TLT and IEF (3.32% and 1.52% over 20 sessions) are the cleaner bets while the bull flattening continues, and the yen carry is the funding risk to hedge. Trim high yield if HYG keeps lagging LQD. The call turns Bullish on credit if the Asian equity bid is absorbed without spreads widening.

anticipatory.title: Iran: a strike or a deal, and the oil premium either way
parts: What Is Priced

The market prices a strike risk and a glut at once. Trump has moved closer to a major war with Iran [[n2902]], and the US military is moving into place for possible strikes [[n2903]]. Oil jumped on geopolitical fears while a massive glut sits at sea [[n5023]]. Brent is at 70.35, up 8.36% over 20 sessions, and WTI at 65.19, up 8.04%; gold is up 5.11% at 5,009.50 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).
Conditional Expression

If the strike goes ahead, own the oil and energy names: USO (79.40, up 10.49% over 20 sessions) and XLE (up 15.08%), with gold (GLD, 458.28) as the hedge. If a deal is reached, the premium comes out: short USO and reduce XLE, which would reverse the 20-session gain. Venezuela's output could climb 30% to 40% this year [[n2941]], which caps the upside even without a deal.
Risk

The risk is the glut. Supply is in surplus at sea [[n5023]], so a short-lived spike in oil would fade fast if the strike is limited. The military build-up is the trigger [[n2935]]; the sizing should respect that a breakdown can move oil quickly in either direction.

anticipatory.title: ECB succession: a credible name, or a political one
parts: What Is Priced

The market prices a succession. Lagarde plans to quit before Macron's term ends, the FT reports [[n2286]], and Reuters puts Knot and De Cos in frame [[n2283]]. The ECB says no decision has been made [[n2298]], and the euro fell after the report [[n2374]]. EUR/USD is at 1.1852, up 1.06% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18).
Conditional Expression

If a policy-consistent successor is named, the euro firms: own EUR/USD on the dip and favour the euro-area banks. If the pick is political, with the political shadow over the process [[n2248]] and Macron's role [[n2303]] on display, short EUR/USD against the dollar, which is supported by the rate debate.
Risk

The risk is that the ECB's credibility is challenged by the process itself. An analysis argues that political meddling over the exit risks undermining the institution [[n2301]], and the euro's reserve-currency story depends on that credibility.

anticipatory.title: Bank of England: the March cut and the inflation print
parts: What Is Priced

The market prices a cut path. UK inflation fell to 3.0%, the lowest in nearly a year [[n2352]], and the Bank of England's cut odds rose as inflation cooled [[n2349]]. Inflation fell to a 10-month low as the BoE mulls further cuts [[n6060]], and it is at its lowest since March 2025 [[n2368]]. Reform UK vows to shake up the Bank of England and the budget watchdog [[n2347]].
Conditional Expression

If the BoE cuts and signals a second, sterling weakens: GBP/USD (1.3564, up 0.92% over 20 sessions, Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18) is the currency expression. The FTSE 100 at 10,686.20, up 5.41% over 20 sessions, is the index expression. If the BoE sounds cautious and the next print runs hot, the cut trade reverses and sterling holds.
Risk

The risk is the composition of the inflation fall. Lower food and fuel prices drove the decline [[n2356]], which can reverse. Reform UK's plan to change the BoE and the OBR [[n2354]] adds an institutional risk that the market has not priced.

anticipatory.title: The Fed's split: cuts, hikes and the Treasury's rate checks
parts: What Is Priced

The market prices a Fed that is divided. The minutes show officials split on where rates should go [[n6621]], with no rush to restart cuts and a possibility of hikes [[n6631]]. The Treasury requested the rate checks [[n6620]], and the Treasury yields rose on the minutes [[n6636]]. Hassett's attack on the Fed's researchers [[n6616]] keeps the independence question live.
Conditional Expression

If the data lets the Fed signal a cut for the spring, own duration (TLT, up 3.32% over 20 sessions) and sell dollar strength against the euro. If the split hardens into a hold, the front end sells off and the dollar firms: short TLT and buy the dollar index (97.70).
Risk

The risk is that independence concerns lift term premia even if cuts come. The Fed's balance-sheet and reserves debate [[n6614]] and the AI-productivity argument [[n6669]] both point to a steeper curve, which would hurt the duration leg first.

catalysts.title: $NVDA — the Feb. 25 print as a guide test
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The dated catalyst is Nvidia's earnings on Feb. 25 [[n1857]], with Wells Fargo seeing a very positive risk-reward setup into the print [[n1919]]. The thesis is that Meta's pact for millions of Nvidia chips [[n4987]] gives visible demand for the next guide, while Nvidia has been reallocating its portfolio, selling its Arm stake [[n4983]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

NVDA closed at 187.98 on 2026-02-18, up 5.57% over 20 sessions and down 0.30% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The hurdle is a guide above consensus. The risk is that a beat with a flat outlook is sold, as Microsoft's record beat was.
Trade Expression

Buy a call spread that runs past the Feb. 25 print [[n1857]]. It is invalidated by a guide that merely matches consensus, or by the Meta chip pact being re-scoped. Take profit into the print if the SOXX group rallies without Nvidia.

catalysts.title: $MU — the AI memory momentum
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Micron is at the centre of AI spending as its shares keep soaring [[n3809]], and Tepper has gone big on Micron, Meta and Alphabet in an AI all-in [[n5005]]. The thesis: memory is the bottleneck that the Nvidia and Meta chip deals depend on, and the stock's momentum is the sign the market is paying for it.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MU closed at 420.95 on 2026-02-18, up 15.33% over 20 sessions and 12.78% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The hurdle is continued pricing power in memory. The risk is that the five-session surge reverses if a guide disappoints.
Trade Expression
Buy MU shares or SOXX on pullbacks. The trade is invalidated if the memory price momentum fades while SMH and SOXX hold, which would show the rally was about positioning rather than the cycle.

catalysts.title: $ASML — the chip-tool cycle
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Global chip tool makers are set for double-digit revenue growth [[n4994]], which is the cycle ASML sells into. The thesis: tool orders lead revenue, so the signal is in the group's guidance before it is in ASML's reported quarter. The risk in the policy line is that US lawmakers want a sales ban on chipmaking tools to China [[n3928]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

ASML closed at 1,468.72 on 2026-02-18, up 10.76% over 20 sessions and 3.45% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The hurdle is continued order strength. The risk is the export-control headline, which hits Dutch export volumes first.
Trade Expression
Buy ASML or SOXX. The trade is invalidated if chip-tool growth slows or the export ban advances, since either would hit equipment orders before chip revenue.

catalysts.title: $XOM — the crude premium and Venezuela
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The catalyst is the Iran decision and the Venezuela supply return. US officials say Venezuela's oil output can climb 30% to 40% this year [[n2941]], while the US military moves toward possible strikes [[n2903]]. The thesis is that Exxon benefits from the geopolitical premium in the near term but faces supply growth from Venezuela, which is a cap on the upside.
Price Hurdle & Risk

XOM closed at 150.68 on 2026-02-18, up 15.5% over 20 sessions and up 3.07% in the prior session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The hurdle is Brent holding above its recent level. The risk is a deal that removes the premium, which the glut at sea makes plausible.
Trade Expression

Mixed: hold the stock but hedge with a put spread or pair against long USO if the strike risk fades. The view is invalidated by a sustained Brent move above the 20-session range, which would confirm the premium is not coming out.

catalysts.title: $IBIT — institutions trim the bitcoin ETF
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Brevan Howard cut its bitcoin ETF holding while expanding options [[n1222]], and Harvard sold bitcoin and bought ether [[n1201]]. The thesis: the institutional holders that built the ETF are trimming into the drawdown, which removes the marginal buyer while bitcoin sits below $70,000 [[n1191]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

IBIT closed at 37.54 on 2026-02-18, down 26.04% over 20 sessions and 3.67% over five (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The hurdle is a recovery of ETF inflows. The risk is that a bitcoin bounce draws the holders back, as Mubadala's added holdings show [[n1194]].
Trade Expression
Buy puts on IBIT or a put spread. The view is invalidated by ETF inflows returning and by bitcoin reclaiming the $70,000 area [[n1191]] on volume.

catalysts.title: $MSFT — the most under-owned mega-cap
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Morgan Stanley calls Microsoft the most under-owned stock in the mega-cap set [[n6693]], and the stock is a split-watch candidate in retail commentary [[n3903]]. The thesis: the record beat is being punished in the tape, and the under-ownership argument is a contrarian entry.
Price Hurdle & Risk

MSFT closed at 399.60 on 2026-02-18, down 12.08% over 20 sessions and up 0.69% in the last session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). The hurdle is a stabilising forward guide. The risk is that the software sell-off [[n5012]] deepens before the guide resets.
Trade Expression

Buy shares in tranches or sell puts below the current level. The view is invalidated if the software de-rating spreads into the group's cloud and AI revenue lines, which would make the under-ownership argument moot.

retail.title: Figma / FIG — the IPO that crashed and jumped
parts: Observed Attention

Figma's stock crashed 81% in the feed's window [[n3840]], then jumped 15% when the company said AI monetisation was accelerating growth [[n1907]]. The earnings offered hope for a turnaround after a revenue surprise [[n1900]]. The attention is about whether the IPO story is over or just repriced.
Motivation & Bias
Retail buys the turnaround: the AI monetisation line is the hook, and the 81% fall is the discount. The bias is recency, since a single good print can make a crashed IPO look cheap again.
Instrument & Risk
Figma shares; the card carries no FIG price, so no level is claimed. The risk is a second fall if the monetisation line does not show up in the next quarter's revenue.

retail.title: SanDisk / SNDK — the storage run
parts: Observed Attention

SanDisk soared 163% in 2026 [[n3839]], and Western Digital sold out all of its 2026 hard-drive production as AI centres scramble [[n3895]]. Retail follows the storage shortage as an AI proxy, with the hook being scarce supply.
Motivation & Bias
Holders are buying the supply squeeze. The bias is extrapolation: a sold-out year is read as a permanent pricing power story, which is the assumption a storage cycle tends to break.
Instrument & Risk
SNDK shares; the card carries no SanDisk price, so no level is claimed. The risk is the cycle: a sold-out 2026 can turn into a price war once new capacity arrives.

retail.title: Robinhood / HOOD — the private-market push
parts: Observed Attention

Robinhood is opening the private market to retail, with a $1B fund to buy pre-IPO shares [[n3865]] and access that the feed reports as a new product [[n3864]]. Retail trading is exploding, the Motley Fool says [[n3848]], and two of Robinhood's top ten holdings are rated best buys by Wall Street [[n6690]].
Motivation & Bias

Retail sees the private fund as a new growth leg. The bias is that the product sounds like a volume story. A critical Guardian piece warns that retail investors are being put at risk by the same access [[n3866]], which is the counter-view.
Instrument & Risk
HOOD shares, with the risk that a sharp reversal in retail trading volumes hits the revenue line. Size to the revenue, not the product headline.

retail.title: Netflix / NFLX — the 55% upside call
parts: Observed Attention

Analysts see 55% upside for Netflix despite its $77 share price [[n3806]], and the stock is down 10.62% over 20 sessions at 77.99 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2026-02-18). Retail reads the analyst upside as a bargain signal, and the price target is the hook.
Motivation & Bias
Retail buys the target, not the earnings. The bias is anchoring: a 55% target is treated as a forecast rather than a view that depends on the next guide.
Instrument & Risk
NFLX shares or short-dated calls. The card gives the close, so the level is 77.99; the risk is that the de-rating continues if the subscriber narrative weakens.
